textbookText: Figure: 9.3.6 Effects of pesticide on human health 5. A variety of wild animals, plants, aquatic organism, microorganism and overall biodiversity (ecological diversity, species diversity and genetic diversity) is harmed by pesticides in long run use. 6. Insect may genetically develop resistance against pesticides due to excessive and prolonged use. Later, such pesticides won’t work. 7. Pest develops resistance to pesticides because of repeated use. As a result, farmers must purchase new and often more expensive pesticides as pests become resistant to older and cheaper ones. The continuous introduction of new pesticides can lead to environmental contamination and harm to non-target organisms, including beneficial insects, wildlife, and even human health. Such condition is called pesticide tread mill or ‘pesticide trap’. Alternative approaches for minimizing the use of pesticides Besides using chemical, there are several other techniques that can be adopted to control pests like crop rotation, biological control (inoculating other organisms in crops which kill or eat pest), use of bio-pesticides (ash, urine of cow, neem extracts etc), mechanical control etc Nowadays an effective strategy for controlling pest called IPM (integrated pest management) which is also recommended by environment activist. This technique adopts all the method of controlling pests with the least use of chemical pesticides.
